 The last two ODIs between India and New Zealand are on November 13 and 15. The Test series begins on November 19. Shubman Gill and  KL Rahul will not play the last two ODI games to prepare for the Tests. In Gill's absence,  Shreyas Iyer , who led India to a 3-2 victory in the T20I series, shall be at the helm.

 Ex-India Stat Not Impressed by the Decision
 One man who is not happy with this decision is former India pacer Dodda Ganesh. Ganesh feels it's not the right choice by Gill and Rahul. For the unversed, it was already known ahead of the tour that they would skip the last two ODI games. But Ganesh believes that due to the lack of game time, it would have been better for them to play a proper cricket match instead of facing thousands of balls in the nets. Rain played a part in all three matches and that limited their exposure. The 3rd game was abandoned without a ball being bowled. 
 © X/ACC 
 What Does Dodda Ganesh Have to Say?
 "Should Gill and KL Rahul rest for the last two ODIs? Considering the amount of game time they've had in the first 3 ODIs I don't think it's a wise idea to pull out of the ODI series. I understand the test match simulation and all that, but a proper game of cricket will prepare you much better than facing thousands of red balls in the net," he posted on X. 
 India Cannot Lose ODI Series
 India are leading the ODI series 2-0 and cannot lose it. One more win or no-result shall clinch it for the Men in Blue. India won the first game by five wickets and the second by four runs as per the DLS method. Gill will also lead the side in the Test series as India aim to end a 17-year-old jinx.

 India's Recent Dismal Test Run in New Zealand
 India last won a Test series on New Zealand soil in 2009. They have also gone winless their last six Tests in New Zealand, having won three and drawn three. The last time they came was in 2020 and were whitewashed 2-0. The last time these two teams met in a Test series, New Zealand whitewashed India 3-0 in the latter's own backyard. 
 What Next for Team India?
 The Test series ends on December 1 to conclude the tour. India then play a three-match ODI series vs Sri Lanka followed by a T20I series against the same opposition in as many games to end 2026.
